3. Briefly stated, the case of the complainant is that accused, who is his maternal uncle, entered into Agreement to Sell dated 27.07.2011 with him for a Plot bearing No. E-63, First Floor, Pandav Nagar,
Delhi, for consideration of Rs.13,75,000/.
It was alleged that complainant made various payments in installments to the accused towards satisfaction of consideration amount on different dates between 23.11.2011 to 19.11.2016.
It was alleged that a total sum of Rs. 10,05,000/ was paid by complainant to the accused in this manner.
However, despite receiving the substantial portion of consideration amount, the accused failed to honour the agreement and execute the sale deed qua plot in question.

sentences.text: It was alleged that the accused extended the date of execution of sale deed on false pretexts and all of a sudden, cancelled the Agreement to Sell vide legal notice dated 07.07.2018 which shows that accused intended to cheat the complainant since beginning.

It was alleged that in response of the legal notice of accused, the complainant also issued a legal notice dated 25.07.2018 to the accused showing his bona-fide qua willingness to execute the sale deed, however, accused opted not to comply with the said notice.

It was alleged that accused unilaterally forfeited the amount of complainant to the tune of Rs. 10,05,000/- and failed to execute the sale deed causing wrongful loss to the complainant and wrongful gain to himself.

Hence, the complaint in question was filed by the complainant against the accused for summoning the accused for AKASH JAIN Date: 2024.10.09 17:39:11 Cr Rev. No:- 55/2021 Naresh Kumar Vs. 4. During pre-summoning evidence, complainant examined himself and Sh. Rakesh Kumar Sharma in support of his allegations as CW-1 and CW-2 respectively.

After hearing arguments on the point of summoning, then Ld. CMM, East District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi was though pleased to dismiss the complaint of the complainant while holding that complainant was never eager or willing to ensure execution of sale deed and that he failed to show any dishonest intention on the part of the accused since inception when he entered into agreement to sell.

8. In the case of Taron Mohan v. State & Anr., 2021 SCC OnLine Del 312 Hon'ble Delhi High Court while discussing the scope of revision jurisdiction was pleased to observe as under:-
"....

entities.text: Taron Mohan v. State & Anr., 2021 SCC OnLine Del 312
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. The scope of interference in a revision petition is extremely narrow.

It is well settled that Section 397 CrPC gives the High Courts or the Sessions Courts jurisdiction to consider the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding inter se an order and as to the regularity of the proceedings of any inferior court.

It is also well settled that while considering the legality, propriety or correctness of a finding or a conclusion, normally the revising court does not dwell at length upon the facts and evidence of the case.

A court in revision considers the material only to satisfy itself about the legality and propriety of the findings, sentence and order and refrains from substituting its own conclusion on an elaborate consideration of evidence...."

9. Further, in the case of Sanjaysinh Ramrao Chavan v. Dattatray Gulabrao Phalke and others, 2015 (3) SCC 123, Hon'ble Apex Court had held that:
".... 14.

entities.text: Sanjaysinh Ramrao Chavan v. Dattatray Gulabrao Phalke and others, 2015 (3) SCC 123
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Unless the order passed by the Magistrate is perverse or the view taken by the court is wholly AKASH JAIN Date: 2024.10.09 17:39:23 Cr Rev. No:- 55/2021 Naresh Kumar Vs. Pramod Kumar Sharma Page No. 4 of 7 unreasonable or there is non- consideration of any relevant material or there is palpable misreading of records, the revisional court is not justified in setting aside the order, merely because another view is possible.

entities.text: Naresh Kumar Vs. Pramod Kumar Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The revisional court is not meant to act as an appellate court.
The whole purpose of the revisional jurisdiction is to preserve the power in the court to do justice in accordance with the principles of criminal jurisprudence.
Revisional power of the court under Section 397 to 401 of Cr.PC is not to be equated with that of an appeal.

Unless the finding of the court, whose decision is sought to be revised, is shown to be perverse or untenable in law or is grossly erroneous or glaringly unreasonable or where the decision is based on no material or where the material facts are wholly ignored or where the judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily or capriciously, the courts may not interfere with decision in exercise of their revisional jurisdiction...."

10. Thus, in the light of aforesaid legal propositions, scope of interference in the revision petition is very limited and the revisionist court is not expected to substitute its own view with that of court below unless the order passed by the Court below suffers from jurisdictional error or patent infirmity/ illegality.

11. In the present case, admittedly an agreement to sell Ex. CW 1/A was executed between complainant and accused on 27.07.2011 vide which accused agreed to sell his flat situated at first floor bearing no. 4 (private number), eastern side built up on area 50 sq. yards on plot bearing No.
E-63, Pandav Nagar, Delhi to the complainant for consideration of Rs.13,75,000/.
However, no date was admittedly fixed in the agreement for execution of sale deed.
In such circumstances, agreement to sell should have been executed within a reasonable time, yet the same was not executed for almost 7 years.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Nothing substantial could be brought on record to suggest that complainant ever insisted the accused to execute the sale deed at earliest.

Last payment made by the complainant to the accused towards partial satisfaction of the considerable amount was on 19.11.2016 i.e. about 2 years prior to cancellation of agreement to sell by the accused on 07.07.2018.
Thus, it cannot be inferred that the complainant was eager and willing to execute the sale deed.

Further, an inference can also not be drawn that the accused intended to cheat the complainant since inception as it was the complainant who delayed in making payments and accused could not be expected to wait for time immemorial for complainant to make entire payment of consideration amount.
12. It is pertinent to note that complainant/ CW-1 deposed in his testimony that accused delayed execution of sale deed on the pretext that property in question was under tenancy and litigation.
However, the property in question was admittedly vacated by the tenant in the year 2014, as per the complaint.
Yet, nothing cogent could be brought on record as to why the complainant did not insist upon execution of sale deed.
Ld. Trial Court thus, rightly observed that complainant failed to show any dishonest intention on the part of the accused since inception when he entered into agreement to sell.

Ld. Trial Court further, suitably placed reliance upon the judgments of M/s Indian Oil Corporation v. NEPC India Ltd. and Ors. (2006) 6 SCC 736 and Md. Ibrahim & Ors. v. State of Bihar & Anr. (2009) 8 SCC 751, vide which it has been held that AKASH Digitally signed by AKASH JAIN JAIN Date: 2024.10.09 17:39:33 +0530 Cr Rev. No:- 55/2021 Naresh Kumar Vs. Pramod Kumar Sharma Page No

Criminal courts cannot be used to arm twist the opposite party when disputes in question are purely civil in nature.

13. Keeping in view the totality of circumstances and the fact that the scope of interference in a revision petition is extremely narrow, this Court finds that Ld. Trial Court was justified in dismissing the complaint under Section 200 Cr.P.C. moved by the complainant.
There is no infirmity, patent illegality or jurisdictional error in the impugned order dated 30.03.2021 which warrants any interference from this Court.
Accordingly, the revision petition stands dismissed.
